hypothesis: the only safe way to normalize this repo is to preserve the entire dirty state before touching branch topology or generated artifacts.
action: created safety branch codex/repo-hardening-safety-20260312T170707, committed the full dirty tree there, and exported tracked/untracked recovery artifacts into /Users/nikitalienov/Documents/thihub-safety-snapshots/20260312T170707/.
expected_signal: the original pre-cleanup state is fully recoverable even after rebuilding the working branch from synced origin/main.
result: confirmed. the safety branch commit 128aa3dbf2e74b8020c2e8bde1eaa2bac030e8a9 preserves the dirty tree and the external snapshot archive contains tracked patches plus the untracked manifest and tarball.
decision: keep the safety branch and external archive untouched while the cleanup branch proceeds.
playbook_note: preserve the full dirty worktree before repo-wide cleanup or branch normalization.

hypothesis: dependency hardening plus source-only pull-forward from the safety snapshot will reduce the repo to a bounded lint surface without bringing generated ops artifacts back into git.
action: updated direct dependencies to current secure-compatible versions, fast-forwarded local main to origin/main, created codex/repo-wide-cleanup-hardening from the synced head, and checked out only source files from the safety snapshot while excluding generated ops output.
expected_signal: the cleanup branch contains useful source deltas plus upgraded manifests, while eslint on the merged state reports a finite, actionable set of issues.
result: confirmed. the branch now carries the dependency refresh and the source-only pull-forward, generated ops files stayed out of the working tree, and eslint reports 37 errors plus 15 warnings instead of an unbounded mixed-state surface.
decision: finish the hardening work on codex/repo-wide-cleanup-hardening and keep generated ops output ignored by policy.
playbook_note: carry forward only source deltas after syncing to origin/main; keep generated ops artifacts out of git.

hypothesis: the remaining repo-wide lint surface can be cleared without weakening rules by fixing render impurity, ref reads, image usage, and narrow typing directly in code.
action: patched the linted files across upload routes, homepage components, article components, hooks, utils, and supporting config; tightened the lint script to `eslint . --max-warnings=0`.
expected_signal: repo-wide lint passes with zero warnings while the build still succeeds.
result: confirmed. `npm run lint` now exits cleanly with zero warnings, and the hardened codepath still builds successfully.
decision: keep lint strict and let the canonical verifier depend on it.
playbook_note: fix render impurity and typing issues directly instead of weakening eslint rules.

hypothesis: a canonical verifier that starts the app through `npm run start` on a fixed port can produce false failures if a stale local server is already running; starting `next` directly and selecting a free port will make runtime verification deterministic.
action: rewrote `scripts/verify-repo.mjs` to resolve a free port by default, launch `next start` directly from the installed next binary, and keep the runtime test flow unchanged.
expected_signal: `npm run verify:repo` passes on the current repo without colliding with stale local listeners.
result: confirmed. after the verifier change, `npm run verify:repo` completed cleanly with regression, perf, admin geometry skip, and audit all green.
decision: keep the free-port direct-next approach as the canonical repo verifier behavior.
playbook_note: when a local verifier boots the app, launch `next` directly and auto-select a free port.

hypothesis: the article page 500 is caused by passing a function-valued custom image loader into `next/image` across a server component boundary; removing that loader and relying on explicit host allowlists will restore the page without reintroducing lint issues.
action: removed the shared passthrough image loader, kept `unoptimized`, and relied on `next.config.ts` `remotePatterns` for the known hosts used by article, quiz, and homepage images.
expected_signal: article pages render successfully again and the stronger local regression run covering article and quiz surfaces passes end-to-end.
result: confirmed. the local article slug stopped 500ing and the strengthened regression run passed with `20` passed, `0` failed, `0` skipped.
decision: do not use function-valued `loader` props from server-rendered component paths; rely on `remotePatterns` plus `unoptimized` where appropriate.
playbook_note: avoid function-valued `next/image` loaders in server-rendered paths; prefer explicit host allowlists plus `unoptimized`.

hypothesis: the repo can be made audit-clean, including dev dependencies, by upgrading direct packages, pinning `markdown-it@14.1.1`, and overriding nested `minimatch` under `@typescript-eslint/typescript-estree`.
action: installed patched dependency versions, added a `package.json` override for `@typescript-eslint/typescript-estree > minimatch@9.0.7`, and reran both prod-only and full audit commands.
expected_signal: `npm audit --omit=dev` and `npm audit --json` both report zero vulnerabilities.
result: confirmed. prod and full audit both report zero vulnerabilities after the final manifest and lockfile updates.
decision: keep the override in place until the upstream dependency chain catches up.
playbook_note: use targeted overrides to clear nested dev-only vulnerabilities when the upstream chain has not yet picked up the patched release.

hypothesis: github actions can reuse the same regression harness as local verification if auth-dependent cases are skipped whenever the required supabase env is not present.
action: updated `scripts/regression-harness.mjs` so admin redirect, quiz admin api auth, and logout checks run only when `NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL` and `NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY` are available; reran `npm run verify:repo` locally after the change.
expected_signal: ci no longer fails because of missing auth env, while local verification with the env present still covers the auth cases.
result: confirmed locally. `npm run verify:repo` still passes with the auth checks active, and the harness now has an explicit skip path for env-less runners.
decision: ship the env-aware harness so github actions can truthfully validate the repo without private runtime secrets.
playbook_note: make shared verifiers skip configuration-dependent checks when the needed env is absent; do not let missing config look like a runtime regression.
